questions.question: A conducting circular loop is placed in X<\/em> – Y <\/em>plane in presence of magnetic field in SI unit. If the radius of the loop is 1m<\/em>, the induced emf in the loop, at time, t<\/em> = 2s<\/em> is n<\/em>πV<\/em>. The value of n<\/em> is……..<\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
$ $ **Question explanation:
$ A$ circular loop of radius 1 m lies in the XY-plane. Magnetic field B = (3t³ $\u$0135 + 3t² k$\u$0302) varies with time. Find the induced emf at t = 2 s in the form nπ volts.

$ $ **Concept:
$ Faraday$’s Law of Induction → ε = – dΦ/dt,
$ where$ magnetic flux Φ = B⊥ × A = (component of B normal to the plane) × (πr²).

$ $ **Solution:
$ Since$ the loop lies in the XY-plane, its area vector is along the z-axis (k$\u$0302).
$ Hence$ only the k-component of B contributes to magnetic flux.

$ $ From given field:
$ B$_z = 3t²

$ $ So flux through loop:
$ $Φ = $B_z$ × A = (3t²) × (π × 1²) = 3πt²

$ $ Induced emf magnitude:
$ $ε = |dΦ/dt| = |d(3πt²)/dt| = |6πt|

$ $ At t = 2 s,
$ $ε = 6π × 2 = 12π volts

$ $ So n = 12.

$ $ **Final Answer:
$ n$ = 12

$ $
$ $
